name: Tapo L510E (EU)

matter.note: TP-Link's spec pages list only Alexa and Google, and we found no CSA listing for the L510E. Not confirmed.

apple_home.note: TP-Link's EU pages list only Alexa and Google, but no official source says Apple Home is unsupported. Not confirmed.

google_home.note: Through the Tapo integration in Google Home, linked from the Tapo app.

smartthings.note: TP-Link's L510E spec pages list only Alexa and Google, and we found no official source naming the L510E for SmartThings. Not confirmed.

home_assistant.note: Listed as supported by the official TP-Link Smart Home integration; needs your TP-Link account credentials.

hubRequired.note: Here this means needing a bridge or hub for basic app control. It joins 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi directly and is controlled from the Tapo app; no hub needed.

localControl.note: Home Assistant's TP-Link integration controls supported devices on the local network, though it authenticates with your TP-Link account credentials.

colorType.note: Fixed warm white, 2700 K; dimmable through the app and cloud only.

lumens.note: 806 lm, comparable to a 60 W incandescent.

bulbBase.note: A60 shape with E27 base for the EU version.

summary: A plain warm white Wi-Fi bulb, the Tapo L510E (EU) works with Alexa and Google Home through TP-Link's skill and Google Home integration, no hub needed. Home Assistant supports it through the official TP-Link Smart Home integration, which controls it on the local network but asks for your TP-Link account credentials. It's an E27 A60 bulb rated at 806 lumens (60 W equivalent), fixed at 2700 K. Apple Home, SmartThings and Matter aren't confirmed.
caveats: Dimming works only through the Tapo app and cloud.
Home Assistant's TP-Link integration needs your TP-Link account credentials, even though control is local.
Apple Home, SmartThings and Matter aren't confirmed; TP-Link's spec pages list only Alexa and Google.
